analysis.title: FX Daily Snapshot: US dollar selling remains contained as Democrats win big
key_insights: Democrats are on track to win both the House and Senate in the US midterms. The FT count at time of writing: 53 Senate seats with 10% of precincts still to report, 223 House seats with 20% to report. Democrats flipped 19 House seats with no Republican flips, and flipped governorships in Texas, Georgia, Iowa and Ohio.
Market reaction is small relative to the scale of the win. DXY is 0.4% weaker, the 10-year UST yield is down 3bps and S&P 500 futures are 0.3% lower. The direction matches expectations.

MUFG sees four reasons for caution. The lame duck session may bring escalation in the Middle East (Iran), Trump's 'Mr. Veto' comment limits what Democrats can pass, AI valuations could come under pressure while further AI deregulation and new tax cuts or spending increases are now unlikely, and Friday's payrolls report matters more for near-term rates and FX.

If Trump does not attack Iran and treats the result as a reason to seek a deal, MUFG says further dollar weakness is much more likely. An Iran escalation would reverse the current drop in the dollar and Treasury yields.
MUFG says the Democratic win could reduce inflation risks and add uncertainty to the optimistic AI outlook, which points to potential further softening in yields and the dollar.

The yen's recent gain is USD-related, and the link between yen and rates remains weak. The 2-year UST yield is down 35bps from its 29 September intraday high while USD/JPY is about one big figure (1 yen) higher.

Two structural flows weigh on the yen that are not tied to rate spreads. NISA-driven household outflows reached JPY 3,949bn of foreign equity purchases on a 3-month sum basis to September (about JPY 16trn or USD 100bn+ annualized), and 12-month net FDI outflows have run JPY 24-28trn (USD 155-180bn) a year for three years.

Washington's opposition to yen weakness is expected to persist, since the midterms are unlikely to change US-Japan relations unless Bessent is removed. Finance Minister Katayama again warned Japan would act 'based on the US-Japan joint statement'. MUFG suspects the yen is close to a turning point.

risk_factors: Trump escalates the Middle East conflict (Iran) during the lame duck session, reversing the dollar and yield declines.
Trump's veto power limits the Democrats' ability to pass policy.
AI-related valuations come under pressure as investors look ahead to the next presidential election.
Friday's payrolls report could outweigh the political shift in driving rates and FX.
Structural yen outflows (NISA, FDI) persist and keep USD/JPY elevated near intervention levels.
vol_and_positioning: Japan investment trust buying of foreign equities on a 3-month sum basis is at a record since the NISA limit was tripled.
47% of Japanese household wealth is held in cash deposits, which supports continued NISA-driven outflows.
geopolitical: US midterm elections: Democrats winning control of the House and Senate, with a lame duck Congress until new members are seated on 3 January.
Middle East: Trump said 'the electorate understands what I am doing in Iran', which MUFG reads as a possible sign of imminent further action.
US-Japan: Washington continues to oppose yen weakness, and Finance Minister Katayama said Japan would act 'based on the US-Japan joint statement'.
Japan demographics: population fell 2.5% in 2025 versus 2020, the largest 5-year decline on record in data back to 1920, per the BoJ Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices.

tension_points.bull_case: Further dollar weakness is much more likely if Trump does not attack Iran and treats the voter repudiation as a reason to seek a deal. The result could also dial down inflation risks and add uncertainty over the AI outlook, pointing to lower yields and a weaker dollar.
tension_points.bear_case: An Iran escalation during the lame duck session would reverse the dollar and Treasury yield declines, Trump's veto limits Democratic policy, and Friday's payrolls report matters more for near-term rates and FX.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Trump attacking Iran during the lame duck session, which MUFG says would reverse the move lower in the dollar and Treasury yields.
